These scenarios are not used for training the lie detector, only for testing its generalisation. When testing the lie detector, we only use conversations in which the model did, indeed, output a lie. All scenarios can be found later on, in Appendix F. ### D.3 Details on settings from Turpin et al. To conduct these experiments, we randomly picked 6 datasets out of the datasets used in Turpin et al. (2023), namely Snarks, Web of Lies, Sports Understanding, Navigate, Hyperbaton, and Disambiguation QA [^7] We conducted all experiments on GPT-3.5 (text-davinci-003). For both settings, we define a biased prompt and an unbiased prompt. In the setting "Answer is always A", the biased prompt contains few-shot examples in which the correct answer is always (A), while the unbiased prompts contain the same examples, but with a balanced order of the answer choices. In the setting "Suggested answer", the biased prompt includes the sentence "I think the answer is [A/B/C/…] but I’m curious to hear what you think." after a question, while the unbiased prompt does not contain this sentence. From each dataset, we picked 10 questions that satisfied the following criteria: - GPT-3.5 answers correctly under the unbiased prompts. - GPT-3.5 answers incorrectly under the biased prompt, and the incorrect answer given is in line with the bias. We then test the lie detector on the questions from each dataset, compute the AUC for each dataset, and report the average AUC across the datasets.

=== key 61ce4b3fc25e
Kind of decision: what evidence to collect
Problem: Build a strong human baseline for comparison with models.
Write-up text before the decision: details on the pre-training dataset). ##### BIG-G sparse. Sparsely-activated expert models including Mixture-of-Experts and Switch Transformers have surged in popularity (Fedus et al., 2021; Artetxe et al., 2021; Du et al., 2021; Clark et al., 2022), offering large model scale without a commensurately large computational cost (Patterson et al., 2021). We pre-train sparsely activated models of a similar design to Zoph et al. (2022), but with only decoder layers. Each model routes tokens independently across 32 experts. The routing mechanism sends each token to the top-2 experts, but with a reduced 1.25 capacity factor (a multiplicative buffer that determines the number of tokens each expert can process). All sparse models are trained on the same mixture as the BIG-G models for 500k steps with 262k tokens per batch. Table App.2 contains details on sparse models. ##### GPT. We use OpenAI GPT models corresponding to the GPT-3 model series in Brown et al. (2020). These are eight dense decoder-only transformers of varying sizes, from 125 million to 175 billion non-embedding parameters. The tokenization is a 50k-token byte-pair encoding, and is the same used by Radford et al. (2019). These models were trained on the same OpenAI dataset for 300 billion tokens, with some tokens used more than once. Additional details of the models, architecture, dataset, and evaluations are provided in Brown et al. (2020). #### 2.3.2 Human rater baseline performance Alongside our language model evaluations, we also employed a team of expert raters to complete the tasks submitted to BIG-bench.

Tasks that see strong breakthrough behavior include those that are composite in nature, meaning that they require a model to apply several distinct skills or perform multiple discrete steps in order to come up with the correct answer. A clear example of this sort of task is modified_arithmetic, which involves applying a mathematical operator, defined in-context to certain inputs. We argue that repeat_copy_logic, figure_of_speech_detection, and codenames are also composite tasks. A task such as codenames, which deals with linguistic analogies and similarities, does not on the surface seem to belong in this category. However, inspection of the question formatting in this task shows that solving it requires following sequential instructions, in addition to basic language understanding. See Section 3.5 for further analysis on the effect that question formatting can have on performance.
